finding.summary: Content/export paths now report `HTTP_ERROR`, not the `ERROR` code the task's acceptance criteria specify
finding.evidence: docs/tasks/active/20260811-cli-upstream-error-envelope-todo.md:44-47 states the acceptance criterion: "An Express-shaped 404 body reaches stderr as {\"error\":{\"code\":\"ERROR\",\"message\":\"HTTP 404\"}} on the content/export paths and {\"error\":{\"code\":\"HTTP_ERROR\",...}} on the import/upload/download paths". The implementation instead defines `UpstreamHttpError { readonly code = 'HTTP_ERROR' }` so `outputError` emits `HTTP_ERROR` on the content/export paths too, and the new test (packages/cli/test/upstream-error.test.ts:219) asserts the new behaviour. Unifying the code may well be the better contract, but the acceptance criterion and the todo doc were not updated to record the deviation, so the documented spec and shipped behaviour now disagree.

verdict.reason: The quoted acceptance criterion exists verbatim at docs/tasks/active/20260811-cli-upstream-error-envelope-todo.md:44-47 and requires code "ERROR" on the content/export paths. The implementation contradicts it: packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:137-146 defines `UpstreamHttpError` with `readonly code = 'HTTP_ERROR'`, thrown by `forwardUpstreamError` (formatter.ts:162-172) — the content/export path — and `errorCode`/`outputError` (formatter.ts:41-63) preserve that code onto stderr. packages/cli/test/upstream-error.test.ts:214-223 asserts `code: 'HTTP_ERROR'` for all six content/export commands, confirming shipped behaviour. Neither the todo doc nor the lessons doc records the deviation, so documented spec and behaviour disagree. This is an unmet acceptance criterion under the spec-conformance lens = major/blocking; no guard, caller, or updated doc reconciles it.

finding.summary: New `HTTP_ERROR` code on content/export paths contradicts the documented error-code contract in README/design doc, which the diff does not update
finding.evidence: packages/cli/README.md:116-120 documents "Typed errors (e.g., INVALID_DOCX, TYPE_MISMATCH, CONFIRMATION_REQ) carry a command-specific code agents can branch on; everything else reports \"ERROR\"". After this change `docs/slides/notes content|export` emit `HTTP_ERROR` (and a `HTTP <status>: <detail>` message) for every non-envelope failure, a new code that agents may branch on. Neither README nor docs/design/cli.md §10's Error Matrix (docs/design/cli.md:1024-1042, which maps backend 5xx/401/403 to exit 2 with codes SYSTEM/UNAUTHORIZED, not exit 1 / HTTP_ERROR) is touched by the diff; the corresponding skill files for content/export also list no HTTP_ERROR.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. The content/export paths do emit a new branchable code: formatter.ts:137-146 defines UpstreamHttpError with code='HTTP_ERROR', thrown by forwardUpstreamError (formatter.ts:162-172) for every non-envelope upstream failure and propagated by errorCode (formatter.ts:41-47) with exit 1; the content/export commands call it at commands/docs.ts:197,249, commands/slides.ts:154,197, commands/notes.ts:148,195. The documented contract is untouched and contradicts this: packages/cli/README.md:116-122 still says typed codes are INVALID_DOCX/TYPE_MISMATCH/CONFIRMATION_REQ and "everything else reports ERROR", and docs/design/cli.md:1024-1042 §10 Error Matrix maps backend 401/403 -> exit 2 UNAUTHORIZED and 5xx -> exit 2 SYSTEM, with no HTTP_ERROR row. I searched wide for a counterexample: a repo-wide case-insensitive grep for http_error across all *.md yields only the two IMPORT skills (packages/cli/skills/docs-import-docx.md:84, slides-import-pptx.md:72), the task docs, and other reviewers' .agent-review artifacts — no content/export skill documents it (skills/docs-read-content.md lists only TYPE_MISMATCH at :86; skills/SKILL.md has no error-code section; slides-read-content.md, docs-export-docx.md, docs-export-pdf.md, slides-export-pptx.md contain no HTTP_ERROR). Independently of the README's "e.g." hedge, the originating issue's own acceptance criterion (docs/tasks/active/20260811-cli-upstream-error-envelope-todo.md:44-47) requires code "ERROR" on the content/export paths and reserves HTTP_ERROR for import/upload/download, so the implementation also fails a named acceptance criterion — a major fit violation under the design-fit rubric. Note the exit-2 classification (UNAUTHORIZED/SYSTEM) has no implementation anywhere in packages/cli/src (grep returns nothing), so that portion of the matrix was already aspirational, but the undocumented new code on content/export is real and unremedied.

finding.summary: Visual-harness change downgrades the font-readiness gate to a warning, the opposite of the posture its own task doc states, and the doc is not updated
finding.evidence: docs/tasks/active/20260811-visual-inter-font-race-todo.md:52-56 ("Notes") justifies the fix on the basis that "The check() wait already hard-fails (10s timeout) if a family never becomes available, so pulling Inter into the same set keeps the existing risk posture: an unreachable fonts.googleapis.com now reports a clear timeout instead of an opaque pixel diff." The diff introduces `settle()` (formatter of warnings) and wraps both the `fonts.check()` poll and the catch-all poll in it, so an unloaded font now yields exactly the opaque pixel diff the task says it is replacing. The plan checklist (lines 44-47) contains no item for making the wait best-effort, and the todo doc is not amended in this diff.

verdict.reason: Verified in-tree. `settle()` at packages/frontend/scripts/verify-visual-browser.mjs:436-444 swallows timeout rejections and only `console.warn`s; it wraps both the `fonts.check()` poll (:395-420) and the catch-all still-loading poll (:421-428), so an unloaded webfont now proceeds to capture and surfaces only as a baseline pixel diff (comparison loop :597-645). That directly contradicts the change's own task doc at docs/tasks/active/20260811-visual-inter-font-race-todo.md:52-56, which justifies the fix by asserting the `check()` wait "already hard-fails (10s timeout)" and that an unreachable fonts.googleapis.com "now reports a clear timeout instead of an opaque pixel diff". The Plan checklist (:44-48) contains no item for making the waits best-effort, and the Notes paragraph is unamended, so the shipped posture reversal is both undocumented and affirmatively mis-documented. No guard elsewhere restores the hard failure — capturePass (:479) screenshots unconditionally after waitForFontsReady. Under the design-fit lens this is a spec/plan-conformance mismatch against the per-task execution plan that CONTRIBUTING.md:60-63 designates as the plan of record, hence major by kind, not refutable.

finding.summary: Unrelated scope creep: a frontend visual-harness font-waiting rewrite is bundled into a CLI error-envelope change
finding.evidence: The diff's stated subject is the CLI upstream-error forwarding helpers (`forwardUpstreamError` / `upstreamErrorJson` in packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts) applied across docs/notes/slides/files. The hunk in packages/frontend/scripts/verify-visual-browser.mjs is a wholly separate concern: it expands VISUAL_FONT_FAMILIES with Inter/Fraunces/JetBrains Mono, adds a VISUAL_FONT_WEIGHTS matrix, adds a catch-all `status !== 'loading'` poll, and relocates `waitForFontsReady(page)` from before the harness-root wait to after the section-ready wait (capturePass). It shares no module, no test, and no acceptance criterion with the CLI work, and it materially changes when screenshots are taken in the visual-baseline lane (a change that can shift/invalidate the ~220 pinned baselines described in docs/design/harness-engineering.md). It should be its own change so it can be reviewed and baselined independently.

verdict.reason: Every element of the hunk exists exactly as described: verify-visual-browser.mjs:350-360 adds Inter/Fraunces/JetBrains Mono to VISUAL_FONT_FAMILIES, :366 adds VISUAL_FONT_WEIGHTS = [400,500,600,700], :421-428 adds the catch-all `face.status !== "loading"` poll, and :479 relocates waitForFontsReady(page) to after the harness-root wait (:467-468) and the section-ready loop (:470-474), with a comment stating the reordering. The CLI half of the branch is genuinely separate: forwardUpstreamError/upstreamErrorJson in packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts applied across commands/docs.ts, commands/notes.ts, commands/slides.ts, docs/import.ts, notes/import.ts, slides/import.ts, files/upload.ts, files/download.ts, with its own task doc. The visual work carries its own distinct task doc (docs/tasks/active/20260811-visual-inter-font-race-todo.md), i.e. a second planned task bundled into the same branch, sharing no module, test, or acceptance criterion with the CLI envelope work. The "~220 pinned baselines" claim is grounded at docs/design/harness-engineering.md:2403, and the visual lane is a gate (harness-engineering.md:195). No refutation ground holds: the code is present, nothing guards it away, and "unrequested scope creep" is explicitly inside this lens's spec-conformance lane. The only mitigating fact — the todo doc justifies the fix as unblocking the CLI branch's verify-browser lane, and CONTRIBUTING.md states no one-task-per-PR rule — softens "unrequested" but does not merge the two concerns, so it is not a counterexample strong enough to drop the finding.

finding.summary: The two new helpers emit different `error.code` for the identical failure condition, splitting the agent-facing contract
finding.evidence: For the same input — a non-envelope upstream failure — `forwardUpstreamError` throws `HTTP <status>`, which `outputError` flattens to `{"error":{"code":"ERROR","message":"HTTP 404"}}` (formatter.ts:46,109), while `upstreamErrorJson` returns `{"error":{"code":"HTTP_ERROR","message":"HTTP 404"}}` (formatter.ts:129). The new test file asserts both divergent shapes (test/upstream-error.test.ts:191 expects `code: 'ERROR'` for `docs content`; :462 expects `code: 'HTTP_ERROR'` for `docs import`). The whole justification in the doc comments is that agents branch on `code`; making the code depend on which command family happened to fail is exactly the ambiguity the change set out to remove. One helper (or one code) would satisfy the same goal.

verdict.reason: The claimed divergence does not exist. `forwardUpstreamError` (formatter.ts:171) throws `UpstreamHttpError`, which carries `readonly code = 'HTTP_ERROR'` as an own property (formatter.ts:137-146). `outputError` uses `errorCode()` (formatter.ts:41-47), which preserves any string `code` on the thrown error and only falls back to `'ERROR'` when none exists — so this path emits `{"error":{"code":"HTTP_ERROR","message":"HTTP 404: …"}}`, byte-identical to `upstreamErrorJson` (formatter.ts:192). Both cited test lines are misquoted: the string `'ERROR'` does not appear anywhere in test/upstream-error.test.ts (grep: no matches); line 191 is `registerSlidesCommand(program);` and line 462 opens the `files upload` case object. The `docs content` command-level case asserts `code: 'HTTP_ERROR'` (test:206, 219), and test:98-109 is an explicit test that `forwardUpstreamError` + `outputError` produces output deep-equal to `upstreamErrorJson` for the same body. The two helpers exist for different reporting mechanisms (thrown-into-`outputError` vs. injected `io.stderr`, per formatter.ts:174-185) but already emit a single unified `code`.
